# Journalist Workflow Tools

As a reporter, you will likely spend most of your time creating and revising content within Desks or your Custom Workspace(s), in addition to monitoring and searching content for research purposes. Once an admin creates an account for you in Superdesk, you will receive an email with login instructions.

If you haven’t already done so, it would be useful to familiarise yourself with the following chapters:

* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#what-is-superdesk?
* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#dashboards-and-widgets
* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#monitoring-tab
* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#heading=h.augg1lln53l3

When you click on Select Workspace (the Desks menu) in the upper-left corner beside the Hamburger menu, a drop-down list of desks you’ve been assigned to should appear. If you don’t see any Desks in this menu, contact your administrator to set them up.

The Dashboard for each Desk will display widgets configured by your editor or admin. You can customise the Dashboard widgets on your Custom Workspace Dashboard.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="The Monitoring View icon" height="45" width="49"></div>

The Monitoring View is a space where journalists or production staff can keep up-to-date on the content in each work Stages, create new items and move content between stages. The Monitoring View can also be set up to show Saved Searches. The content of the Monitoring View tab is set up by your desk administrator, in the Desks section of the Hamburger menu.

### Content Workflow

{% stepper %}
{% step %}
### Create a new item

* Make sure you’re on the Desk where the item should be created (check the Desks menu at the top of the Superdesk interface), or create in your Personal Space if it’s not intended to be shared right away.
* Click the Monitoring icon (second icon on the Workspace Panel) to enter the Monitoring workspace.
* Click the Create icon in the upper-right corner. The list of creatable items depends on the content profiles assigned to your desk.
{% endstep %}

{% step %}
### Create and save an article

* Select a content profile or template to create from.
* Enter metadata and some text, then click SAVE in the top-right corner to save as a draft. Articles are saved to the Desk you’re currently working on (if in a custom workspace, saved to the current user’s default desk).
* You can keep an article open but minimise it using the minimise icon beside SAVE.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="The minimise icon" height="44" width="48"></div>
{% endstep %}

{% step %}
### Locks and autosave

* If you don’t close the article, it locks to prevent other users from updating it (senior staff can override).
* All open items remain visible in the Workspace Bar at the bottom of the interface.
* If a user session hasn’t been updated in four hours, the session is terminated and the lock is dropped.
* A red stripe next to the article entry in the Monitoring tab denotes a locked item.
* Changes are autosaved on the server and locally; if you lose connection you can restore work once reconnected (some issues possible if modified during disconnection).

<div align="left"><img src="../../.gitbook/assets/image135 03feb00d5dbc9af8bfd0a6e828bfbd8b.png" alt=""></div>
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

### Research & Multi-Pane Workflow

The Search feature allows users to navigate multimedia from any repository Superdesk is aware of: various news agency feeds, RSS, emails and other sources. These sources are set up by the Superdesk administrator. If you cannot find items from a desired source, notify your administrator.

Superdesk’s multi-pane workflow enables users to have a Monitoring or Search window for research open at the same time as an article entry. This makes it convenient to work on an article and switch context to look up information in an archive, for example. Users can also have multiple article entry windows open simultaneously.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="The search icon" height="62" width="74"></div>

### Monitoring Issues & Saved Searches

{% stepper %}
{% step %}
### Save an Advanced Search

* Click the Search icon on the Workspace Panel and set parameters for your Advanced Search.
* After performing the search, click the blue Save Search button that appears at the bottom of the screen.
* Turn on the Global Read toggle if you want the Saved Search available for use in Monitoring widgets outside your Custom Workspace. (If only used in your Custom Workspace, Global Read is not needed.)
* You can save searches even if they currently return no content; you’ll be alerted when matching content arrives.

<div align="left"><img src="../../.gitbook/assets/image261 9059e228691080670a1f7e9c95de473c.png" alt=""></div>
{% endstep %}

{% step %}
### Add a Saved Search as a Monitoring widget

* Click the house-shaped Dashboard icon on the Workspace Panel.
* Click Create in the top-right corner to add a new widget.
* Select Monitoring Widget → Add this Widget → Done.
* To adjust settings, click the gear in the top-right corner of the widget on the Dashboard.
* In the Saved Searches tab, choose from Global Saved Searches and toggle them on/off.
* Use Reorder Sections to drag and drop multiple searches and desk Stages into the preferred order.
* Adjust how many items to display for each section of the Monitoring widget.
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

### Updating Content

To resume working on an article after it’s been closed, find it via Search in the Monitoring view of the Desk.

![](<../../.gitbook/assets/image23 1268af2171104121281e747d99b452de.png>)

From the Monitoring View you can use the Quick Search Filter (click the search icon in the top-left of the Monitoring pane) to rapidly filter through thousands of items within a Saved Search.

When the desired article appears in a list, hover over it to reveal an Action Menu and click Edit to open the item in a new pane.

### Bundling Images and Text Items Together

There are several ways to bundle images and text together:

* Create a package and insert both images and text items into the package.
* Insert images directly into the main body of an article.
* Add images as attachments when an article is open for editing.

Ask your Editor which method they prefer. See these sections elsewhere in the manual for details:

* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#packages
* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#making-new-articles
* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#attachments

### Sending Drafts

{% stepper %}
{% step %}
### Send items from Personal Space to a Desk

* If you created an item in your Personal Space and are satisfied with it, click the ‘Send to’ button in the top-right of the article editing window to send it to a Desk for review.
* If you created an article on a Desk, it will automatically be visible to others.
* Depending on permissions, you may be able to send it to the publishing queue using the Send to/Publish button.
* If not ready to send, click SAVE, then CLOSE to revisit later.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="The Send to / Publish icon" height="43" width="43"></div>
{% endstep %}

{% step %}
### Move an item between stages or publish

* Click the ‘Send to’ button on the right-hand corner of the article editing window.
* In the pop-up menu, select destination Desk and work stage (e.g., Bureau chief in, Bureau out).
* Use this button to move items between States of a Desk or to another desk. Stages are set up by your administrator to organise items within a Desk.
* You can also set an Embargo notice and a publishing schedule. Note: an Embargo does not prevent publishing.
* Publishing can be scheduled. Once Published, items can only be updated or killed.
{% endstep %}

{% step %}
### Updates and Kills

* Update: create a new article with the same metadata (bylines, dateline, headline, abstract, priority, urgency, place, subject, category). The takekey becomes “update”. Updates cannot be performed on picture items or packages.
* Kill: used to stop clients from using content you sent them (they must remove the content once you do this). Useful for e.g., court stories with a subsequent non-publication order.
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

![](<../../.gitbook/assets/image386 a5f43f705c02d504832cba73b2fdc404.png>)

### Spiking

Spiking an item means marking it for removal from the Desk workflow without deleting the information (so it can be reused later). To view all spiked items, click on the Spiked Items icon on the Workspace Panel.

To Spike an item, open the Action menu of the article and select Spike Item. Note that published items cannot be Spiked. Items spiked from your Personal Space are permanently deleted.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="The Spike icon" height="44" width="47"></div>

### Other Useful Features & Tools

#### Templates

Save any article including metadata as a template: open the Action menu at the top of the article editing window and select Save as template. You’ll be prompted to name the template and assign it to a Desk.

![](<../../.gitbook/assets/image248 a9cffa4c6004f8237a94642a5c4eb23d.png>)

* Creation templates create content with a specific profile (e.g., court template).
* Highlights templates configure elements (Headline, Byline, Abstract, etc.) from multiple articles to be displayed as flat/digest files.

#### Multiedit

The Multiedit button lets you toggle between multiple open content items and display two news items side-by-side in editing mode. Enable Multiedit from the action menu at the top of the article editing window. You can select up to 12 articles to open in Multiedit mode at once.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="This is the multiedit icon" height="42" width="53"></div>

#### Highlights

The Highlight icon on the Workspace Panel allows viewing Highlight lists used for content indexes, top-10 lists, section features, and user-curated lists. Highlights can be generated automatically or curated manually, and can be scheduled for publication or distribution. Most journalists will not have permission to add items to a Highlight list.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="This is the Highlights icon" height="46" width="48"></div>

#### Versioning

While an item is open for editing, click the Versioning icon in the Editor Sidebar to display previous saves or revert to earlier versions of a content item.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="This is the versioning icon" height="47" width="44"></div>

#### Annotations

Annotations let journalists add additional information to articles. They can be created from the Hamburger menu (Annotations Library) or within the editor while creating an article.

![](<../../.gitbook/assets/image183 02d7e2ea3144322c58421599f070689f.png>)

To add an annotation to text in the body, highlight the text and click the annotations button. Read more at:

* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#using-the-annotations-feature

### Custom Workspaces and Personal Space

Custom Workspaces are configurable individual workspaces accessible from the Desks menu. They have their own Dashboards and Monitoring tabs, making it possible to monitor several Desks in one place—ideal for users working on more than one Desk.

Customising your Custom Workspace Dashboard lets you monitor several projects without switching Desks. Only you can access your Custom Workspaces, so you can tailor Dashboard and Monitoring settings to your workflow. Dashboards of Desks have widgets determined by the Desk manager.

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="The Personal Space icon" height="46" width="47"></div>

Personal Space is an icon on the Workspace Panel. Clicking it displays all articles and items you created in your Personal Space. Only you can view or edit items there. To create a new Personal Item, click the Create icon in the top-right of Personal Space. Send Personal Items to a Desk workflow using the purple ‘Send to’ button in the article editing window.

### User Profile Settings

Click your user icon in the upper-right corner and select Profile to view and adjust profile settings. You can set preferences and contact information, view your privileges, and view your activity stream. User privileges are set by administrators.

### Comments

When an article is open for editing, users can add Comments to each news item with Twitter-like @mentions. This is useful for alerting other Desks or users to content quickly.

![](<../../.gitbook/assets/image29 c87837ba1e469ef665cc2a89ff391909.png>) ![](<../../.gitbook/assets/image59 f2955da5405ccbdef7de70968afe31c3.png>)

Comments appear in the Editor Sidebar when an article is open (use the Comments button). Inline Comments can also be added to the Body of a news item; see:

* https://superdesk.github.io/superdesk-docs/docs/user-guide/journalist-workflow-tools/#using-the-inline-comments-feature

<div align="left"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="This is the Comments button in the Editor Sidebar." height="40" width="42"></div>

### Mark for User (since Superdesk v1.33)

The Mark for User feature keeps track of news items that require a user’s attention. Items can be marked for users from:

* the action menu of an item in any list view (Monitoring or Highlights),
* the action menu in the Editor or Preview pane,
* icons at the top of the Monitoring pane when multiple items are selected.

![](<../../.gitbook/assets/image39 73beb0f06b0fc6b885146d047c5292db.png>)

Users can access items marked for them from the menu left of their user icon, or by clicking Marked for Me at the top of the Monitoring pane for the current Desk. The info bubble on Marked for Me shows how many items are assigned in general or within the current Desk.

<img src="../../.gitbook/assets/unknown (21).png" alt="" height="40" width="139">

Clicking an item in the Marked for Me list will open it in the Editor unless it’s locked by another user. Spiked items and locked items cannot be marked. Only users with the mark-for-user privilege can use this action.

When marking content for a user, the online status indicator is shown on user avatars in the selection list so you can see if the target user is online. The marked user receives an in-app notification and an email. Marking creates a new version of the content item so the user receives the latest copy and unsaved changes are not lost.
